messages:
mia: Hey folks, BrightFrame reporting a sudden vectors/sec collapse since ~2026-03-17 00:30 UTC. tokens/sec for text endpoints are normal, embeddings return 200 but vec throughput is ~4x lower.

eva: Customer BF-881: they said nothing changed on their side except switching model variant last week. Sending repro payload in a sec.

mia: Repro curl they ran:
`curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rb-embed-1536", "input":["sample text"]}'`

jordan: Can you dump kube logs and GPU queue depth? Sounds like runtime batching/queueing.

mia: quick logs from their pod (trimmed):
```
INFO embedding_service: processed 32 vectors in 12.2s -> 2.62 vec/s
GPU queue depth: 14 pending
WARN kv_cache: eviction_count=340
WARN kernel: falling back to fallback-kernel=fp32-fallback for model rb-embed-1536
```

sam: Interesting: tokens/sec fine but kvpath/kernel fallback triggered. Fallback kernels are ~3-4x slower. Why did it pick fallback? quantization/shape mismatch maybe.

ingrid: Infra telemetry shows p95 GPU util went from 62% -> 88% at 00:31 but not full saturation. Memory page faults spiked on node gpu-12, autoscaler created 2 pods that hung in init for ~60s.

jordan: Any auth/billing noise? If a key rotation flooded retries it could bloat queues.

mia: There were auth 401 spikes ~00:28 (rotate) ~1200 401s over 5m; billing webhook returned 429s at 00:29 for a short window. But the vec slowdown persisted after auth stabilized.

sam: Did the customer change embedding dim? rb-embed-1536 moved from 1024 -> 1536 a week ago; kernel selection tables might not have been updated. If kernel descriptor mismatch -> fallback.

mia: Customer confirmed they upgraded model variant a week ago.

jordan: Quick repro idea: try smaller batch sizes; large batches + fallback kernel = long GC-like stalls and head-of-line blocking.

mia: They tried reducing batch_size from 128 -> 16: vec/s jumped 2.62 -> 8.1. So large batch window is amplifying the slow path.

sam: That strongly points to scheduling/batching misestimation or wrong kernel chosen for that shape. Also check for `kernel=fp32-fallback` logs in runtime.

ingrid: Rolling back the recent autoscaler policy change that increased the batch window for the embeddings pool to restore previous behavior. @jordan initiating rollback.

deploy-bot: Roll started by ingrid: autoscaler-policy-rollback (id: rp-2026-03-17).

jordan: Next steps for runtime/ML:
- capture pprof on affected runtime pods during repro
- export kv_cache hit/miss and eviction counters
- look for kernel selection audit logs (match model arch + seq_len -> kernel id)
- add temporary per-pool max-batch cap (max_batch=64) to avoid large queue formation

mia: I'll ask BrightFrame for a short maintenance window to repro while we collect traces. Also sharing their minimal curl and sample outputs with eng.

eva: Please share ETA, RM needs an update.

sam: Hypothesis summary: kernel descriptor mismatch after model variant change (dim 1536) triggered slow fallback kernel; combined with a batch-window increase and a transient auth/billing retry storm caused large batches to queue and starve the fast path -> measured vectors/sec drop while tokens/sec (different path) unaffected.

jordan: Agreed. I'll add kernel guards and surfacing logs for `kernel=fp32-fallback` and push short-term cap. If we confirm, plan to backfill kernel selection table and mark that model shape as fast-kernel.

mia: Action items assigned: me -> coord with customer + reproduce window; jordan -> pprof + kernel logs + temp cap; ingrid -> rollback autoscaler change fully; sam -> verify kernel selection table and quant profiles. Will update thread after repro. :thumbsup:

eva: Thanks, looking forward to the follow-up.
